paras.en: "By being cognizant of how they shape the landscape of fear experienced by carnivores and their prey species, humans can proactively adjust their behavior and spatial use of landscapes in ways that can transform the human-carnivore relationship from one of conflict to one of coexistence," he writes.
paras.zh: 他写道：“通过认识到它们如何塑造食肉动物及其猎物所经历的恐惧景观，人类可以主动调整自己的行为和对景观的空间利用，从而将人与食肉动物的关系从冲突关系转变为共存关系。”

paras.en: "And thereby rebalance the attendant cascading effects that human fear effects have on wildlife communities and ecosystems."
paras.zh: “从而重新平衡人类恐惧对野生动物群落和生态系统产生的连锁效应。”

paras.en: All three papers have been published in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 所有三篇论文均发表在《当代生物学》上。

paras.en: You can read the bear paper here, the mountain lion paper here, and Schmitz's dispatch here.
paras.zh: 您可以在这里阅读熊报、山狮报和施密茨的快报。

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

paras.en: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat
paras.zh: 科学家发现了一种普通抗抑郁药难以治疗的新型抑郁症

paras.en: Experts hope discovery will lead to alternative and more targeted behavioural and medical treatments, notably in young people in the early stages of these disorders.
paras.zh: 专家希望这一发现将带来替代性的、更有针对性的行为和医学治疗，特别是对于处于这些疾病早期阶段的年轻人。

paras.en: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现了一种新的抑郁症亚型，可能影响近四分之一的重度、复发性或持续性抑郁症患者。它被称为“昼夜节律抑制”，与人体的生物钟有关，并与夜猫子倾向、过度睡眠、持续疲惫和更严重的症状有关。传统的抗抑郁药物通常对这些人效果较差，这可能解释了为什么有些人难以寻求缓解。

paras.en: A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.
paras.zh: 一种新发现的抑郁症可能有助于解释为什么有些人很难从常用的抗抑郁药中找到缓解方法。 Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

paras.en: The discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.
paras.zh: 这一发现是对 10,000 多名澳大利亚抑郁症患者的临床和遗传信息进行分析得出的。这项研究主要针对患有严重、复发或持续性抑郁症的人，近四分之一的参与者表现出这种新发现的亚型的特征。

paras.en: Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.
paras.zh: 昼夜节律抑制与人体的 24 小时生物钟有关，它有助于调节我们何时感到清醒和何时感到困倦。患有这种抑郁症的人往往对常见的基于血清素的抗抑郁药反应较差。然而，针对参与控制昼夜节律的大脑回路的治疗，包括褪黑激素、针对褪黑激素的抗抑郁药和光疗法，可能会提供更有效的选择。

paras.en: Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.
paras.zh: 发表在《英国精神病学杂志》上的研究结果揭示了与这种亚型相关的遗传因素，并为为什么广泛使用的药物如 SSRIs（选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）对某些患者效果较差提供了可能的解释。

paras.en: A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied
paras.zh: 一种隐藏的抑郁症影响了近四分之一的研究患者

paras.en: To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.
paras.zh: 为了调查不同形式抑郁症之间的生物学差异，研究人员检查了通过全国性澳大利亚抑郁症遗传学研究收集的信息。他们的分析包括 10,000 多名抑郁症患者的临床病史和遗传数据。

paras.en: The researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现近 25% 的人（2,604 名参与者）患有昼夜节律抑郁症。一些可识别的模式将这些人与其他抑郁症患者区分开来。

paras.en: Those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.
paras.zh: 具有昼夜节律亚型的人更有可能经历抑郁症的季节性变化，在抑郁时睡眠时间更长，尽管在床上的时间更长，但醒来时仍感到精疲力竭。他们也更有可能是夜猫子，这意味着他们自然更喜欢熬夜并在一天中晚些时候起床。

paras.en: The differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.
paras.zh: 差异不仅限于睡眠模式。这些人的抑郁症通常在生命早期就开始出现，而且他们的症状往往更严重（例如躁狂和更高程度的自杀念头）。基因分析还显示，人们更容易患炎症和心血管健康问题，以及包括注意力缺陷多动症（ADHD）在内的主要神经发育障碍。

paras.en: First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:
paras.zh: 第一作者、悉尼大学大脑与思维中心的 Emiliana Tonini 博士说：

paras.en: "Our research has identified circadian depression as a new subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.
paras.zh: “我们的研究已将昼夜节律抑郁症确定为一种新的亚型，在我们的研究中，约四分之一的人患有严重、复发或持续性抑郁症。

paras.en: "Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them."
paras.zh: “抑郁症不是一种统一的疾病，了解不同亚型的特征意味着我们可以让人们尽早获得对他们最有效的治疗。”

paras.en: Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective
paras.zh: 为什么普通的抗抑郁药效果可能较差

paras.en: One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.
paras.zh: 这一发现最重要的意义之一涉及如何治疗抑郁症。

paras.en: Medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.
paras.zh: SSRI 和 SNRI（血清素和去甲肾上腺素再摄取抑制剂）等药物通常是为诊断为抑郁症的患者提供的首选治疗方法。这些药物通过影响大脑中有助于调节情绪的化学信使发挥作用。

paras.en: However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员发现这些药物对于昼夜节律抑郁症患者的效果往往较差。患有这种亚型的人也会经历更多的副作用，这表明传统的抗抑郁药可能不是适合每个人的最佳初始方法。

paras.en: Because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.
paras.zh: 由于昼夜节律抑制与人体的内部时钟密切相关，因此旨在影响该时钟的疗法可能特别有用。例如，光疗法利用受控的强光照射来帮助调节生物节律。褪黑激素是一种与身体何时准备睡眠有关的激素，而针对褪黑激素途径的抗抑郁药也可能是相关的治疗选择。

paras.en: Co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:
paras.zh: 大脑与思维中心的共同资深作者雅各布·克劳斯博士解释说：

paras.en: "Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.
paras.zh: “由于昼夜节律抑郁与人们的体内生物钟有关，因此针对昼夜节律的治疗，例如光疗和褪黑激素，可能更相关，临床医生应该更早地对患有这种表现的人进行这些治疗。

paras.en: "For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is important to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances."
paras.zh: “对于那些发现抗抑郁药对他们不起作用的人来说，向您的临床医生咨询有关您个人情况的建议非常重要。”

paras.en: A New Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People
paras.zh: 一种新方法可以改善年轻人的抑郁症治疗

paras.en: Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.
paras.zh: 尽早认识昼夜节律抑郁症对于年轻患者尤其重要，否则他们可能会花费宝贵的时间尝试不太适合其特定形式抑郁症的药物。

paras.en: Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.
paras.zh: 大脑与思维中心联合主任、临床精神病学家 Ian Hickie 教授警告说，未能识别年轻人的这种亚型可能会导致早期治疗不成功和不必要的副作用。

paras.en: The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.
paras.zh: 研究结果强调了认识到抑郁症不是单一、统一的病症的重要性。不同的生物学机制可能会导致类似的症状，这意味着对一个人有效的治疗可能对另一个人提供的益处要少得多。

paras.en: By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.
paras.zh: 通过识别抑郁症与昼夜节律密切相关的患者，临床医生也许能够更早地提供更有针对性的治疗，而不是依赖于为每个人提供相同的初始药物治疗方法。

paras.en: "We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.
paras.zh: “我们真的希望年轻人在病程早期接受最合适的治疗。

paras.en: "Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition."
paras.zh: “大多数年轻人将首先接受 SSRIs，但至少有四分之一的年轻人有更好的以昼夜节律为中心的医疗和行为选择来帮助治疗和管理他们的病情。”

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由悉尼大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
